page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture. The instance is powered by an Ampere Altra processor operating at a sustained clock speed of 3.0 GHz. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated physical cores corresponding to 4 vCPUs, utilizing a single thread per core topology without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 16.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core.

The server configuration does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, featuring zero GPUs. Operating system and persistent data storage require external network-attached block volumes. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the Ampere Altra architecture dedicates one execution thread per physical core, execution pipelines operate without contention from hyperthreaded neighbors, yielding predictable execution times across compute tasks.

From an efficiency perspective, the Arm-based Ampere Altra platform offers high core density and low thermal design power, resulting in favorable resource economics for general compute. A notable architectural tradeoff involves software compatibility, as binaries and toolchains must support the 64-bit Arm instruction set rather than x86_64. Additionally, the absence of bundled local storage necessitates reliance on remote block storage latency and bandwidth. This server configuration fits general-purpose cloud workloads including web serving, microservices, containerized applications, development environments, and native Arm build systems.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine provisioned on the 64-bit Arm architecture. Powered by an Ampere Altra processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, the instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped directly to 4 physical cores with a single thread per core, avoiding resource contention from simultaneous multithreading. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data, and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address. The Arm-based infrastructure delivers favorable compute density and operational cost efficiency relative to traditional architectures. However, deploying on this server requires Arm-compatible software stacks, and I/O depends entirely on network-attached storage. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.4-16 fits mid-tier general-purpose enterprise tasks, including microservice hosting, container runtimes, web application servers, and continuous integration pipelines targeting 64-bit Arm environments.
